headers.rom:B0FD: sub_B0FD. LDA #$3B / STA ram_213A -- seeds the timer-expiry 'final buzzer' sound-effect countdown (see rom:213A). Called once from sub_97C6's L_97E8 tail, immediately before falling into TriggerMatchEnd -- so it fires exactly once per timer-expiry match end, never for the other two causes.
headers.rom:9D23: sub_9D23. The match/round reset: zeroes a block of 0x36 bytes at ram_00BD (timers/state), zeroes several possession and phase cells, sets ram_22C2 = 2 (a fixed constant read elsewhere as a rotation-phase reference, see rom:E372), then re-seeds the goal geometry via two calls to sub_9CF5 (rom:9CF5) -- (X=ram_22CA, Y=0) for entity 9's own slot, (X=ram_22C9, Y=9) for entity 18's slot (Y is added directly to the $0094 base, which is itself ram_008B+9 = entity 9 -- so Y=9 lands on entity 9+9 = entity 18, the RotationPhase-selected duplicate confirmed on rom:9DD0). Also seeds fixed starting positions for the player and ball arrays (entities 0-2) and resets PossessionState. Reached at true match start (via sub_9929's tail) and again once per theme-song loop thereafter (via sub_9D18, rom:9D18 -- CORRECTED there, not once per goal) -- the second path is what makes the goal-shrink mechanic live during a match rather than only at its start.
headers.rom:E378: sub_E378. Part of the dispatcher tail already documented on rom:E372 (RotationPhaseToFragment) and rom:97EE -- reached from $E30D's chain. Alternates which player it processes via X = (ram_0042 EOR 1) AND 1 (ram_0042 is the free-running frame counter incremented in DliHandler_GridMusic, so this simply alternates player 0 on one frame and player 1 the next). Reads that player's RotationPhase and a position boundary (ram_00A9,X compared against #$1B, the same shape as sub_9E7A's own boundary check) to pick between two lookup tables, dat_E422 ({6,18}) and dat_E424 ({12,24}), indexed by player -- the result becomes the goalpost slot number fed to the chain of four sub_BD80 calls (L_E2EC/L_E314/L_E3AE/L_E3D6) alongside the player-index calls already documented on rom:BD80. Confirms sub_BD80 is shared between ship-fragment placement and goalpost placement within the same four call sites, not two separate systems.
headers.rom:D14A: sub_D14A. Runs once a frame (from the main VEC_996F-rooted chain at $9A0E). Chooses between the match-end spin and ordinary Rotosnap: if EndSequenceTimer is nonzero (spin in progress), calls AdvanceRotationPhase (the forced-fast path); otherwise calls SteerTowardTarget (rom:D1DA). CONFIRMED this is why the two never run in the same frame -- not a coincidence of their internal gating, a direct either/or dispatch.
headers.rom:DB46: RotateOrbitVector. Applies one rotation step to the 3-byte fixed-point velocity/position pair (ram_00C0/00C3/00C6 and ram_00DB/00DE/00E1) using a delta computed by the caller (ram_004C/004D/004F/0050/0052/0053), with the rotation direction/cross-term selected by X's sign (sub_DB8F vs. its mirror at L_DBCF) -- textbook 2D rotation-matrix application, not simple translation. This is the mechanical half of BallOrbitPhysics (rom:DA66); the angle/rate is decided there.
headers.rom:E372: RotationPhaseToFragment. Y = (ram_22C2 - RotationPhase) AND 3 -- ram_22C2 is a fixed constant (#$02, set once at match reset by sub_9D23 and never written again), so this index tracks RotationPhase directly. dat_E428[Y] is stored into ram_231E, which PickSpinFragment (rom:CEC1) reads. CORRECTION: this isn't purely rotation-phase-driven -- the same dispatcher block (starting around $E30D, this is only its tail) reads ram_22D9,X (the possession-contest flag PossessionCheck sets for the non-holding player, see rom:D8EC) at $E343 and again at $E364, folding contest state into the fragment choice alongside phase. Not fully unwound -- worth revisiting if the exact visual difference during a contested ball matters.
headers.rom:CEC1: PickSpinFragment. Reduces ram_231E to one of three fragment ids ($B6/$B9/$BC, via BMI/BVS on ram_231E's bits) into ram_005F, then falls into PokeDisplayListByte to write it -- and the two bytes after it ($DD and ram_0065) -- into the live display list. CONFIRMED LIVE: playing back run-01.inp and watching these exact writes during the spin (frames 6900-7050) caught PC=$CEEC (this routine) and PC=$CE18 (a sibling call site at $CE00) writing exactly $B6/$B9/$BC into the new zone entries documented on rom:9800, at the same 2-frame cadence the screenshots show the silhouette changing.
headers.rom:CEDE: PokeDisplayListByte. LDY ram_0068,X (an offset) / LDA dat_C680,X,dat_C697,X (a pointer table, X selects which live zone entry) -> STA (ram_0058),Y. A generic 'write one byte into the live display list' primitive, not specific to the spin -- reused by whatever else needs to poke a zone entry, so X/Y at the call site are what actually target it at the ship.
headers.rom:B15E: Unreached by the static tracer but CONFIRMED EXECUTING in all three recordings (read-tap on the window, tools/live-slots.lua: 902/300/539 fetches, first at frame 133, i.e. during attract boot). Reads POKEY RANDOM at $400A and writes the $21xx audio block, then JMPs back toward LoadThemeSong -- an attract-mode variant of the song loader. Disassembled from the rom:B15E entry, not hand-decoded.
